examples.en: I make up for lost sleep all at once on the weekend.

examples.ko: 지난달 적자를 이번 달 매출로 벌충했어요.
examples.en: We made up for last month's deficit with this month's sales.

examples.ko: 늦은 만큼 오늘 밤에 일해서 벌충할게요.
examples.en: I'll make up for being late by working tonight.
How should we make up for this loss?

examples.ko: 수업에 빠진 부분은 숙제로 벌충해도 돼요?
examples.en: Can I make up for the class I missed with homework?
I'm covering the shortfall in money with a part-time job.

explain: '메우다', '보충하다'와 비슷하지만, 손해나 부족, 잘못을 다른 것으로 채워서 맞춘다는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '~을/를 ~(으)로 벌충하다' 형태로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '만회하다', '메우다'도 같이 들려요.
explain_en: It is close to '메우다' and '보충하다', but it strongly means balancing out a loss, shortage or mistake with something else. It usually appears as '~을/를 ~(으)로 벌충하다'. In daily talk you will also hear '만회하다' and '메우다'.

examples.en: I got stung by a bee and my arm swelled up.
I got stung by a bee in the mountains and it really hurts.

examples.ko: 손등에 벌침이 박혀 있어서 빼 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: A stinger was stuck in the back of my hand, so I asked someone to pull it out.

examples.ko: 저는 벌침 알레르기가 있어서 늘 조심해요.
examples.en: I'm allergic to bee stings, so I'm always careful.

examples.ko: 벌침을 빼려면 카드로 살살 긁어 보세요.
examples.en: To remove the stinger, gently scrape it with a card.
My younger sibling went to the hospital because of a bee sting.

explain: 다쳤다고 말할 때는 '벌에 쏘이다'가 더 일상적이에요. '벌침'은 쏘는 침 자체나 그 상처를 말할 때 자연스러워요. '벌침에 쏘이다', '벌침을 빼다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: When you say you got hurt, '벌에 쏘이다' is the more everyday phrase. '벌침' sounds natural when you mean the stinger itself or the sting wound. It pairs with verbs like '벌침에 쏘이다' and '벌침을 빼다'.

en: suddenly and abruptly; with a gulp

examples.ko: 동생은 목이 말랐는지 물을 벌컥벌컥 마셨어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling must have been thirsty and gulped down the water.

examples.ko: 갑자기 현관문이 벌컥 열려서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The front door suddenly flew open and I was startled.

examples.ko: 아버지가 벌컥 화를 내셔서 아무도 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: Dad suddenly flew into a rage and nobody could say a word.

examples.ko: 노크도 없이 방문을 벌컥 열면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What are you doing, flinging the door open without even knocking?
I downed some cold water in one go and now I feel refreshed.

examples.ko: 친구가 아무 말 없이 벌컥 일어나서 나가 버렸어요.
examples.en: My friend suddenly stood up without a word and walked out.

explain: 문을 열거나 화를 낼 때처럼 갑자기 확 하는 느낌이에요. 물을 마실 때는 '벌컥벌컥'처럼 겹쳐서 계속 들이켜는 모습을 나타내요. 눈물이 갑자기 쏟아질 때는 '벌컥'이 아니라 '왈칵'을 써요.
explain_en: It gives a feeling of something happening abruptly and forcefully, like a door flung open or a sudden burst of anger. For drinking, it is doubled as '벌컥벌컥' to show continuous gulping. For tears suddenly welling up, use '왈칵' instead.

examples.en: The government started a nationwide campaign to save energy.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 범국민적 관심을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: This matter is drawing nationwide attention.
Many people took part in the nationwide campaign.
Protecting the environment takes an effort by the whole nation.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 노래는 범국민적 사랑을 받았어요.
examples.en: That singer's song was loved by the whole nation.
A consensus among the whole nation has to be reached first.

explain: 뉴스나 연설에서 '범국민적 운동/노력/관심'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '온 국민이', '전 국민이'라고 말하는 편이에요. '범세계적', '범시민적'처럼 '범-'이 붙으면 '전체가 함께'라는 느낌이 돼요.
explain_en: It is placed before a noun in news and speeches, as in '범국민적 운동/노력/관심'. In everyday talk people say '온 국민이' or '전 국민이' instead. With '범-', as in '범세계적', it carries the sense of everyone taking part together.

examples.ko: 법을 어긴 범법자는 처벌을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Lawbreakers have to be punished.

examples.ko: 신호를 무시하는 사람도 작은 범법자가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even someone who ignores traffic signals can become a minor lawbreaker.
The police are chasing the lawbreaker who ran away.
Anyone who breaks the law becomes a lawbreaker.
He wasn't a lawbreaker from the start either.
I think even lawbreakers have human rights.

explain: '범죄자'는 큰 범죄를 저지른 사람이라는 느낌이 강하고, '범법자'는 법을 어긴 사람 전체를 넓게 말해요. 그래서 교통법규처럼 가벼운 위반에도 쓸 수 있어요. 뉴스나 토론에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: '범죄자' strongly suggests someone who committed a serious crime, while '범법자' broadly covers anyone who broke the law. So it can be used even for minor violations like traffic rules. It appears often in news and debates.

examples.en: That child has an extraordinary look in the eyes.

examples.ko: 범상한 사람이라면 그런 결정을 못 했을 거예요.
examples.en: An ordinary person couldn't have made that decision.
From the first impression, he was no ordinary person.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 범상해 보여도 사실 아주 유명해요.
examples.en: This painting looks ordinary, but it is actually very famous.
The atmosphere felt unusual, so I was careful.

examples.ko: 그는 이 일을 범상하게 넘기지 않았어요.
examples.en: He did not let this matter pass as something ordinary.

explain: 대부분 '범상치 않다/범상하지 않다'로 써서 '보통이 아니다, 뭔가 특별하다'는 놀람이나 칭찬을 나타내요. '범상하다'만 쓰는 경우는 글에서 가끔 보여요. 일상에서는 '평범하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the negative, '범상치 않다/범상하지 않다', to express that someone or something is out of the ordinary, with surprise or praise. The plain affirmative '범상하다' shows up only occasionally in writing. In daily speech, '평범하다' is how you say ordinary.

examples.en: I saw an old model of a sailing ship at the museum.
In the old days, people crossed the sea on sailing ships.
A sailing ship only moves forward when the wind blows.

examples.ko: 항구에 하얀 범선이 한 척 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A white sailing ship came into the harbor.

examples.ko: 범선에는 돛이 여러 개 달려 있어요.
examples.en: A sailing ship has several sails.
Most pirate ships in movies are sailing ships.

explain: 우리말로는 '돛단배'라고도 하는데, 범선은 큰 배를 말할 때 더 자연스러워요. 엔진으로 가는 배와 구별할 때도 써요. 배는 '한 척, 두 척'으로 세요.
explain_en: Native Korean also has '돛단배', but '범선' sounds more natural for a large ship. It is also used to set it apart from engine-powered ships. Ships are counted with '척', as in '한 척, 두 척'.

examples.en: Climate change is a worldwide problem.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 범세계적 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: That singer is gaining worldwide popularity.
It's hard to solve without global cooperation.
This brand is known all over the world.
Infectious diseases require a global response.

examples.ko: 범세계적 규모의 행사라서 준비할 것이 많아요.
examples.en: It's a global-scale event, so there is a lot to prepare.

explain: '세계적인'이 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이고, '범세계적'은 온 세상이 함께 관련된다는 무게가 있어서 뉴스나 글에서 많이 보여요. 주로 '문제, 협력, 대응' 같은 말 앞에 와요.
explain_en: '세계적인' is the easier everyday word, while '범세계적' carries the weight of the whole world being involved and shows up in news and writing. It mostly comes before words like '문제', '협력' and '대응'.

examples.en: There were too many errors in today's match.
We can only win if we cut down on errors.
It was a shame that an error came at a crucial moment.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 범실 때문에 세트를 내줬어요.
examples.en: Our team gave up the set because of errors.
One service error changed the flow of the game.
The players were nervous and made errors one after another.

explain: 주로 배구 같은 운동 경기에서 선수가 하는 실수를 말할 때 써요. 야구에서는 '실책'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 그냥 '실수'라고 해요. '범실이 나오다', '범실을 줄이다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for a player's mistake in sports such as volleyball. In baseball people say '실책', and in daily life simply '실수'. It appears in phrases like '범실이 나오다' and '범실을 줄이다'.

examples.ko: 어른께 물건을 드릴 때 두 손으로 드리는 것도 예의범절 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Handing something to an elder with both hands is also part of good manners.

examples.ko: 예의범절은 나라마다 달라서 여행 전에 알아 두면 좋아요.
examples.en: Etiquette differs from country to country, so it's good to learn it before traveling.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 예의범절이 몸에 배어 있어요.
examples.en: That child has good manners ingrained.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁은 범절이 엄격해서 항상 긴장돼요.
examples.en: Grandma's house is strict about manners, so I'm always on edge.

examples.ko: 식사 범절을 배우려고 책을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a book to learn table manners.

examples.ko: 집안 범절을 지키라고 아버지가 자주 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My father often tells me to follow the family's rules of conduct.

explain: 대부분 '예의범절'로 붙여 써요. '범절'만 따로 말하면 집안 어른이 말하는 듯한 옛 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '예절'이나 '매너'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the compound '예의범절'. On its own, '범절' sounds a bit old-fashioned, like something an elder in the family would say. In daily conversation '예절' or '매너' is more common.

examples.ko: 그분은 너무 대단해서 아무도 범접하지 못해요.
examples.en: That person is so great that nobody can come close.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 실력에는 아무도 범접할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Nobody can match that player's skill.

examples.ko: 범접하기 어려운 분위기에 말을 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: The atmosphere was so intimidating that I couldn't speak to them.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 너무 멋있어서 범접할 수 없는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: That actor is so cool that he feels unapproachable.

examples.ko: 그 요리사는 아무도 범접할 수 없는 경지에 올랐어요.
examples.en: That chef has reached a level no one else can approach.

examples.ko: 처음에는 선배가 범접하기 힘든 사람 같았어요.
examples.en: At first, my senior seemed like someone hard to approach.

explain: 거의 항상 '범접할 수 없다', '범접하기 어렵다'처럼 부정이나 어려움과 함께 써요. 지위나 실력이 높거나 위엄이 있어서 가까이 다가갈 수 없다는 느낌이고, 보통 감탄이나 존경이 담겨요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with negation or difficulty, as in '범접할 수 없다' or '범접하기 어렵다'. It means someone's status, skill or dignity is so high that you cannot get close, and it usually carries admiration or respect.

examples.en: The criminal escaped the law and fled abroad.
The legal net is tight, so it's hard to slip through.

examples.ko: 그는 결국 법망에 걸려 처벌을 받았어요.
examples.en: He was finally caught by the law and punished.
Some people cleverly exploit the loopholes of the law.
This case exposed the gaps in the legal net.
There are still many people who slipped through the law.

explain: 법을 그물에 비유한 말이라서 '법망을 피하다', '법망을 빠져나가다', '법망에 걸리다'처럼 그물에 어울리는 동사와 같이 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 나오고 일상 대화에서는 드물어요.
explain_en: It pictures the law as a net, so it goes with net-like verbs such as '법망을 피하다', '법망을 빠져나가다' and '법망에 걸리다'. It appears often in news articles but rarely in everyday conversation.

examples.en: The whole family is bustling around because guests are coming.
The kids are playing noisily in the yard.

examples.ko: 시험 날 아침부터 집 안이 법석거렸어요.
examples.en: The house was in a flurry from the morning of the exam.
It's nothing serious, so why are you making such a fuss?
We bustled around all day getting ready for the move.
The market is so bustling with people that my head is spinning.

explain: 여럿이 시끄럽고 바쁘게 움직이거나, 별일 아닌데 좀 지나치게 호들갑을 떠는 느낌이에요. '법석대다', '법석이다'도 같은 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 '법석을 떨다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It describes people moving around noisily and busily, or making a bit too much fuss over something minor. '법석대다' and '법석이다' mean the same thing. In daily speech, '법석을 떨다' is also widely used.

examples.en: The kids are running around noisily and it's chaotic.

examples.ko: 부엌에서는 아침부터 법석법석 음식을 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: They've been busily cooking in the kitchen since morning.
The puppy is going wild in front of the door.

examples.ko: 손님이 온다고 법석법석 청소를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: We're cleaning in a flurry because guests are coming.
The market is noisy and bustling with people.

examples.ko: 아침부터 온 가족이 법석법석 짐을 싸고 있어요.
examples.en: The whole family has been packing in a rush since morning.

explain: 시끌시끌 떠들며 바쁘게 움직이는 모습이에요. '북적북적'은 사람이 많아서 붐비는 것에 초점이 있고, '법석법석'은 소란스럽게 움직이는 데 초점이 있어요. 뒤에 '떠들다, 뛰다, 청소하다' 같은 동작이 와요.
explain_en: It shows people moving around busily while making a racket. '북적북적' focuses on a place being crowded, whereas '법석법석' focuses on the noisy bustle. Action verbs like '떠들다', '뛰다' and '청소하다' follow it.

examples.en: It's nothing serious, so why are you making such a fuss?

examples.ko: 새로 온 강아지 때문에 우리 집은 하루 종일 법석였어요.
examples.en: Our house was in a commotion all day because of the new puppy.
I can hear the kids making a racket in the classroom.
It's the day before the holiday, so the market is bustling with people.
My younger sibling has been making a fuss since morning about going on a trip.
Don't make a fuss, just wait calmly.

explain: '법석거리다', '법석대다'와 같은 말이에요. 사람이 많거나 일이 있어서 시끄럽고 어수선한 상태를 나타내고, 별일 아닌 일에 지나치게 소란을 떨 때는 가볍게 핀잔하는 느낌도 있어요. '법석을 떨다'라는 말도 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It means the same as '법석거리다' and '법석대다'. It describes a noisy, chaotic state caused by many people or some event, and when someone overreacts to something minor it can sound mildly scolding. Also learn the related phrase '법석을 떨다'.

examples.en: The government said it would enact the new rule into law.
That proposal has not yet been made into law.
The National Assembly legislated the animal protection measures.

examples.ko: 환경 기준을 법제화하자는 목소리가 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: Calls to put environmental standards into law are growing.

examples.ko: 이 내용을 법제화하려면 시간이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: It will take more time to make this content into law.

examples.ko: 안전 수칙을 법제화한 뒤 사고가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Accidents decreased after the safety rules were made into law.

explain: 뉴스나 토론에서 '~을 법제화하다' 형태로 자주 나와요. 일상 말로는 '법으로 정하다'라고 하면 쉬워요. 이미 있는 관행이나 약속을 법으로 만들 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It often appears in news and debates in the form '~을 법제화하다'. In plain everyday speech you can say '법으로 정하다'. It fits well when turning an existing practice or agreement into law.

examples.ko: 동생은 선물을 받고 하루 종일 벙글벙글했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling beamed all day after getting the present.
The baby beams when it sees its mom.

examples.ko: 무슨 좋은 일이 있어요? 아침부터 벙글벙글하네요.
examples.en: Did something good happen? You've been beaming since this morning.
Dad smiled broadly at the news that I passed.

examples.ko: 벙글벙글하는 얼굴을 보니 저도 기분이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: Seeing that beaming face made me feel good too.
My friend was beaming because it was payday, and bought us a meal.

explain: 소리는 내지 않고 입을 크게 벌려 환하게 웃는 모습이에요. '벙글벙글 웃다'처럼 '웃다' 앞에 부사로 붙여서도 말해요. '싱글벙글'도 비슷하게 기분 좋은 웃음을 나타내요.
explain_en: It shows someone smiling brightly with a wide mouth but without making a sound. It is also used as an adverb before '웃다', as in '벙글벙글 웃다'. '싱글벙글' expresses a similar happy smile.

examples.en: The baby looked at me and smiled.
Grandma smiled and waved her hand.

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해서는 아무도 입을 벙긋도 안 했어요.
examples.en: Nobody breathed a word about that matter.
When the photographer spoke, everyone smiled.

examples.ko: 선생님은 아이를 보며 벙긋 웃어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher looked at the child and gave a smile.

examples.ko: 친구가 그 얘기를 듣고 벙긋 미소를 지었어요.
examples.en: My friend heard the story and broke into a smile.

explain: 소리 없이 입을 살짝 벌려 웃는 모습이에요. 웃음뿐 아니라 '입을 벙긋도 안 하다'처럼 입을 열어 말하려는 동작에도 써요. 이 경우는 거의 부정형으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 일에 대해서는 아무도 입도 벙긋 안 했어요.
phrases.en: Nobody said a word about that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 한마디도 하지 않는다는 굳은 표현이에요. 주로 부정형으로 쓰고, 비밀이나 침묵을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set expression meaning not saying a single word. It is used mostly in the negative and fits secrets or silence.

explain_en: It shows a silent smile with the mouth opening slightly. Besides smiles, it is also used for the motion of opening the mouth to speak, as in '입을 벙긋도 안 하다'. In that sense it is almost always used in the negative.

examples.en: I was dumbfounded by the sudden news.

examples.ko: 무슨 말인지 몰라서 한참 벙벙해 있었어요.
examples.en: I didn't understand what was said and stood there bewildered for a while.
My friend suddenly started crying and I was dumbstruck too.
I'm in a daze at the news that I won the lottery.

examples.ko: 벙벙한 표정으로 서 있는 그에게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: I explained things to him as he stood there looking bewildered.

examples.ko: 너무 놀라서 한동안 벙벙하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was so shocked that I stood there dazed for a while.

explain: 거의 '어안이 벙벙하다'로 써요. 갑자기 놀라거나 어이가 없어서 말이 안 나오고 멍한 상태예요. '당황하다'는 허둥대는 느낌이 있고, '벙벙하다'는 멍하니 굳은 느낌에 가까워요.

phrases.example: 시험에 합격했다는 말을 듣고 어안이 벙벙했어요.
phrases.en: I was dumbfounded when I heard I had passed the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻밖의 일에 놀라 말문이 막힌 상태를 나타내는 굳은 표현이에요. 좋은 일과 나쁜 일 모두에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set expression for being struck speechless by something unexpected. It can be used for both good and bad news.

explain_en: It is almost always used in '어안이 벙벙하다'. It describes being so surprised or taken aback that you cannot speak and feel dazed. '당황하다' suggests flustered flailing, while '벙벙하다' is closer to being frozen in a blank daze.

examples.ko: 아기가 엄마를 보고 벙실벙실 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is looking at Mom and smiling happily.
Grandpa smiled broadly as he looked at his grandchild.

examples.ko: 상을 받은 동생이 하루 종일 벙실벙실 웃고 다녀요.
examples.en: My younger sibling who won the prize goes around smiling all day.
The children saw the presents and beamed.

examples.ko: 벙실벙실 웃는 얼굴을 보니 저도 행복해졌어요.
examples.en: Seeing that beaming face made me happy too.

examples.ko: 그는 칭찬을 듣고 벙실벙실 기분 좋게 웃었어요.
examples.en: He heard the compliment and smiled happily.

explain: 입을 크게 벌리고 소리 없이 부드럽게 웃는 모습이에요. 아기나 마음씨 좋은 사람의 웃음에 잘 어울려요. '방실방실'은 더 작고 귀여운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It shows a soft, silent smile with the mouth wide open. It suits a baby or a good-natured person. '방실방실' feels smaller and cuter.
